label: Original/delimiter step, a non-trigger input after >=2 trigger tokens (1,3,u,j,v,p,2,h) were seen
explanation: Graded, distributed candidate unit. It fires mostly in the input phase (59% of mass, peaking at t=3-5) and at the <DEL> step (32% of mass; 18% of delimiter steps). It is driven by a history of trigger tokens (1, 3, u, j, v, p, 2, h, especially as the first token or two steps back) and fires when the current input is a different token such as <DEL>, w, r, e, d, s, t, x, l. The strongest activations are at <DEL> in short sequences whose first tokens are digits 1/3 or u/j/v. It almost never fires at t=0, and rarely in the copy phase (9% of mass) or when the current input is itself a trigger or a repeat of an earlier token. It is not a clean conjunction: about 40% of the mass falls outside the predicate, and precision is about 0.33 because many steps with trigger history stay inactive, particularly late in long sequences.
